title: Why Is My Dryer Not Drying Clothes? Common Causes and Fixes

seo.title: Dryer Not Drying Clothes: Causes and Fixes
seo.meta_description: If the drum turns but clothes stay damp, check load size, lint filter, vent airflow, heat, and cycle behavior before assuming an internal failure.
seo.search_intent: Diagnose a dryer that runs but dries poorly by prioritizing airflow restrictions and loss of heat with clear safety boundaries.

excerpt: A dryer can tumble normally and still dry badly. The most useful split is whether it produces heat and whether that heated air can leave the machine freely.
content_html:
If the drum turns but clothes stay damp, answer two questions: is there heat, and is there strong airflow? That split separates many vent problems from heating failures.

Start with the load and lint filter

An overloaded drum dries slowly because air cannot move between garments. Clean the lint screen and retry with a smaller load.

Check airflow at the exterior vent

While keeping clear of hot and moving parts, confirm that the exterior flap opens and air exits strongly. A crushed, overly long, or lint-loaded duct increases drying time and fire risk.

If there is no heat, stop repeating cycles

An electric dryer can sometimes tumble even when part of its heating supply is missing. A gas dryer may have an ignition or fuel issue. Do not bypass safety devices or open gas components.

Very hot but still damp often points back to airflow

Hot clothing, unusually long cycles, and an excessively hot cabinet are consistent with heat being trapped. Stop the dryer and address venting before continued use.

When service is the next step

If the load, filter, and complete vent path are good but heat is absent or cycles remain abnormal, internal diagnosis may involve heaters, sensors, thermal fuses, or gas components.

faq.question: Does a clean lint screen rule out a vent problem?
faq.answer: No. The duct behind the dryer and the exterior termination can still be restricted.

faq.question: Why are clothes very hot but still damp?
faq.answer: That pattern can indicate poor airflow; stop if the dryer is overheating and inspect the vent path.

faq.question: Should I just run longer cycles?
faq.answer: Not until you know why drying time increased, especially because restricted venting can become a fire hazard.
